test_set: none: data/splits.json has 16 train, 3 validation, 0 test recordings

fps.about: The real server (python -m shinobi.server, its own port) over the WebSocket, fed the camera fixtures (1280x720, 15 fps, the user's recordings spliced into sign sequences, looping) like a browser: one frame in flight, JPEG 80. Stage timings are the server's own FrameState.timings (ms). 'no effect' = frames without a running effect. The machine was shared with other agents' work while measuring.

loro.about: Leave-one-recording-out on the 19 split recordings (train + validation; there is no test set): train.py's random forest (n_estimators 300, min_samples_leaf 2, balanced) on mirrored + jittered copies, every 2nd frame, refitted without the held-out recording, scored on all its frames with a hand after the first 0.5 s. A sign with ONE recording is absent from training when its recording is held out: its frames cannot be right, so those rows show only what it is mistaken for and are left out of the metrics.

montecarlo.about: SequenceMatcher alone (the app's class, current rules: per-jutsu counters, a wrong sign keeps the progress, 7 s limit in Live, none in Practice) fed one uniformly random sign every 1.8-3.6 s, for 200.0 simulated hours. It shows how often signs made in NO particular order complete a jutsu by chance. Recognition is assumed perfect here; the spliced random streams of the 'sequences' part include the real recognisers.

negatives.about: Hands that make NO sign of the app; the right answer for every frame is idle. Never-trained clips (claw, OK sign, two open palms) + the 2 held-out idle recordings (validation set).

sequences.about: No guided sequence takes exist (data/sequences is missing), so performances are SPLICED from the single-sign recordings: an idle lead-in, each sign held 1.6-2.6 s, 0.4-1.2 s of idle between signs (real transitions between seals are not in the data), 3 s of idle after. Windows are random; the held-out validation recording is used where a sign has one (idle, rasengan_palm). Everything else comes from TRAIN recordings, see 'signs' per jutsu.
